title: Income rises

predict.q: Average incomes rise 10%. Demand for a value-range pasta has a YED of −0.5. What happens to the demand curve for the value-range pasta?

options.s: It shifts right: richer people buy more of everything.
options.fb: Richer people buy more of some goods but less of inferior ones; YED is negative here.

options.s: It shifts left: demand falls at every price.
options.fb: YED −0.5 × 10% = −5%: about 5% less pasta is demanded at every price, so equilibrium price and quantity fall.

options.s: Price rises, so there is a movement up the curve.
options.fb: Income is not the good's price; a change in income shifts the whole curve, not a movement along it.

options.s: Nothing: income does not affect demand.
options.fb: Income is a determinant of demand; YED of −0.5 means demand responds.

task: Move the income slider to +10% and watch both demand curves (a normal good and the value-range pasta).

target.do: Move the income slider to +10%, then press Check.

takeaway: A rise in income shifts demand for a normal good right and for an inferior good left.
